title: BlockMetadata, DecodedBlock, ScannedBlock missing Clone and PartialEq
description:
The three public result types (BlockMetadata, DecodedBlock, ScannedBlock) derive only Debug. They are missing Clone and PartialEq, which are standard derives for data-carrying types in library crates.

Missing Clone means:
- Callers cannot store a decoded block in multiple places without an explicit reconstruction.
- Cannot use block.clone() in test helpers, iterators that need to yield twice, or any place that requires ownership duplication.

Missing PartialEq means:
- Callers cannot compare two decoded blocks with ==.
- Tests must compare fields individually (block.data == expected_data, block.metadata.filename == ...) instead of asserting block == expected_block.
- Property-based tests and snapshot tests are harder to write.

UuError already derives PartialEq (error.rs line 2), so there is precedent in this crate for deriving equality.

All fields (Vec<u8>, String, u32, usize, bool) implement both Clone and PartialEq, so no manual implementation is required.

Fix: Add #[derive(Clone, PartialEq)] to BlockMetadata, DecodedBlock, and ScannedBlock in lib.rs.
